Synopsis:
Dialogue with the Toll collector.She will continuously, endlessly demand gold from the player. You can convince her to let you pass (hard persuade), or you will have to fight  (once you stop giving it gold, or once you run out of gold).

Cluster Contexts:
- TWN_Tollhouse_TollhouseMaster.json: You're confronting Gerringothe Thorm — a persistent toll collector at a gate who repeatedly demands gold and will not stop repeating the demand until you pay, persuade him, or force him. Off‑screen you may be at the road into Baldur’s Gate or a Den checkpoint; your current coin pouch and any companions present matter because the scene expects either a hard Persuade to let you pass or repeated payments until you run out. The collector’s pleading can read as weary or desperate, but—consistent with nearby Den con artists—this may be a grift: exposed, he can drop the act and take any “fool’s” coin. If you refuse to keep paying (or exhaust your gold), the encounter escalates into combat.
- LOW_GuildSmugglers_Smuggler.json: A smuggler watches you approach and wants you to leave.Player can convince smuggler to sell the goods, or player initiates combat.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelsExtort.json: You killed Nere off‑screen and never completed the duergar mutineers quest, so a duergar warband led by Kirgrath has intercepted you to demand “restitution” for the trouble you caused. Kirgrath postures violently but is wary of your fighting ability—his men have been stripping the area for loot and intend to haul off prisoners (gnomes/slaves) unless paid or resisted. The clan is jittery about Moonrise forces or other duergar arriving, so they’re in a rush to leave. Companions (Karlach in the samples) may press you to free the captives; your choices are to pay them, try to talk Kirgrath down, or fight the duergar.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelGreedyExtort.json: You’ve already killed Nere but never completed the duergar mutineers quest, so the duergar treat his death as your crime and demand compensation for the trouble you caused. Elder Brithvar and his clan are on site, tense and ready to leave Moonrise Towers with prisoners and loot — they explicitly claim any gnome slaves as “clan property.” Companions (Karlach appears in the scene; others like Gale might speak up) can argue for the captives or push toward violence. Off‑screen, Nere’s corpse and the captured gnomes/servants (possibly including the elevator gnome Skickpit or other enslaved folk) are present as leverage, and reinforcements or further duergar reprisals could arrive if you refuse to pay or try to bargain. Your immediate choices are to pay them, persuade/intimidate them into letting you live and freeing the captives, or fight.
- WYR_WyrmRock_SouthBridgeGuard_001.json: First guard at the checkpoint. You can1) bribe the guard2) show Coronation Access Pass3) show Urgent Report for Duke Ravengard
